method: Direct English translation of normalized Arabic auto-captions by the editing assistant. No external machine-translation service and no audiovisual review.

segments.text: Peace be upon you. Emotional attachment may be
the most dangerous way a jinn—whether a devil
or a Muslim—enters people's lives. Such a
relationship may also begin at a human's initiative.
This episode will examine that subject.
It is a very sensitive and serious one. First,
can there be an emotional relationship between
these two different kinds of beings? If so,
what are its limits and possible consequences?
Our first aim is to build awareness of important
questions of belief that touch people's lives.
Awareness means prevention first, and perhaps
also dealing with things that could happen
to someone unprepared—even someone who does not believe in them.
We also want to answer questions from young people
who are curious about other worlds, especially
when they look into these subjects and find answers
only within very different religious and intellectual traditions.
So this episode matters even to people
who are not interested in the subject. Anyone
could become a victim, or at least
this could happen to someone we know and care about.
This particular subject also leaves considerable room
for superstition and legend. There can be confusion
even among some preachers. Let me stress at the outset:
do [not] listen to this episode with your children present.
segments.review_notes: Provisional negation: the raw ASR lacks 'not' but the immediately following sentence explicitly says the episode is unsuitable for children. Brackets make the editorial repair visible; audio check required.

segments.text: It is entirely unsuitable for children. I will discuss
three questions in this episode: the possibility
of affection and romantic attachment between
humans and jinn; then the possibility
of a physical, intimate relationship between them;
and, if such a relationship is possible,
the possibility of conception and birth.
I will discuss whether each of these can happen,
then whether it is lawful or unlawful. This episode
draws together several years of research. I will summarize
the religious rulings, what scholars have said,
and the evidence in our revealed texts. I will also cite
views from other religions, peoples and cultures.
Another important source is testimony I receive
from people I know and trust. We will also consider
similar material from popular culture:
films, anime and other works. But first,
in the opening section, I will consider one example
of the culture of denial found among a broad segment
of Muslims today. Then we will begin
examining the foundations of the subject.
First, let us consider an example of denial. Please
listen with me to this short clip,
less than a minute long, from Ahmad al-Shugairi.
It is from episode six of the third season
of Khawatir, fourteen years ago. We will listen,
then comment on it.
[Al-Shugairi:] Another example of charlatanism and superstition I came across
segments.review_notes: Embedded Khawatir excerpt begins; speaker label added for clarity. Original broadcast remains unverified.

segments.text: was something astonishing. I was amazed to read it:
the subject of jinn marrying humans. Unfortunately, there are books
in our libraries across the Arab world, books printed
recently. This book in front of me was printed in 2003,
in the twenty-first century, yet it says: humans and jinn may intermarry
and have children together. What is this backwardness?
Have we reached such a level of intellectual decline
that we now believe a jinn could marry
a human?
If we open the door to this kind of talk,
we open the door to unlawful sex in the Muslim world. Any
woman could turn up pregnant, and when her father asks,
she could say, 'I am married to a jinn!' What is this
backwardness?
[Presenter:] As you saw, I showed the whole passage
segments.review_notes: Return to al-Sabeel presenter after embedded excerpt.

segments.text: so as not to take his words out of context. He calls it charlatanism:
a book printed in the twenty-first century mentions
intermarriage and childbirth. Then he asks, 'What is this backwardness?
What is this decline?' First, he does not name
the book he is reading. Even in
the editing, they covered its cover.
Giving him the benefit of the doubt, it also seems
he does not know that the line he read was taken
by the author of this book from Ibn
Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him. It is copied word for word
from Ibn Taymiyyah. We will return to this quotation;
it will come up again later. In Majmu Fatawa Ibn
Taymiyyah, volume [unclear], page 40, he says that humans
segments.review_notes: ASR omits volume number. Independent research located Majmu al-fatawa 19:39–40; subtitle leaves spoken gap explicit.

segments.text: and jinn may intermarry and have a child together; this is frequent
and well known, and scholars have mentioned and discussed it,
and so on. In any case, I suspect
al-Shugairi had not actually read the book in his hands.
Perhaps he had not even read a whole page
or noticed which source the passage was taken from,
or whether there was a footnote. He did not notice any of that.
He was simply very angry, and responded to
this author in this insulting manner. Then
in the following passage, which you can
check in the episode, he says that the result of
all this thinking is not merely to justify unlawful sex.
His central idea is also that
the influence of devils must be limited to whispering. He cites
a clip of Sheikh Ali Gomaa. As you know, Sheikh Ali Gomaa
segments.review_notes: Following characterizations of Ali Gomaa, modernism and Mu'tazila are the presenter's claims, not independent editorial findings.

segments.text: combines Sufism, including a degree of
excess in Sufism, with its opposite:
an excessive emphasis on material, scientific explanations,
the school of Muhammad Abduh. We discussed this
school before; some call it the modernist school,
and discussed its role in promoting these ideas: denying everything
to do with magic, reducing it to illusion and denying
that it has any reality, and also limiting Satan's influence
to whispering. Historically, this is the Mu'tazilite school.
The problem is that al-Shugairi, like the sheikhs of this
age—or preachers, rather than scholars, of course—
uses this logical fallacy: I feel something
is a problem, namely justifying unlawful sex,
so I reject it and deny its very existence. I deny the possibility
of this relationship taking place because I dislike
its consequences. You may find this logical fallacy
in an atheist too. I am not equating them;
I am discussing a mentality and an idea. An atheist, for example,
dislikes the idea of [remaining eternally] in Hell, so he dislikes God
segments.review_notes: ASR reads الخروج (leaving); context appears to require الخلود (eternal remaining). Provisional bracketed repair; audio check required.

segments.text: Himself and therefore denies His existence. He does not
merely rebel against a God or religion he dislikes,
or against all religions. Instead, he denies God's very existence,
and with it the existence of all these religions,
even though anything's objective existence is independent
of whether I like it. North Korea
has a backward system. I dislike that system,
but I do not deny its existence. I say I dislike it,
and that is that. Another problem is that
throughout this programme, Ahmad al-Shugairi
said in every opening, word for word, 'I am not a scholar,
a sheikh or a mufti, but a student of knowledge.' Even
the expression 'student of knowledge' is misunderstood by someone
who is not one. It means you have entered
a systematic course of seeking knowledge and begun studying,
so you possess a student's tools. But someone making
these mistakes cannot possibly have begun
that process. The episode I mentioned
is entitled Khuzabalat—'Nonsense'—and itself contained
a great deal of nonsense. As we said, it was
around fifteen years ago. People of my generation remember
those days: satellite channels openly featured magic
and charlatanism. He draws conclusions from the superstitions
and nonsense he mentioned in the episode, which we agree
were nonsense—not actual magic, but superstitions.
He groups those with other things, including this
clip, and calls all of it nonsense. Incidentally,
al-Shugairi was one of the few young people
given a platform on which to present
their opinions. In those days, there was no internet
segments.review_notes: ASR literally says there was no internet/YouTube, but immediately mentions online forums. Bracketed contextual qualification is provisional; do not treat as verified technology history.

segments.text: or YouTube [as we know them]; there were forums
read by thousands. But when MBC
gives someone this platform—and it is a secular channel—
it wants to present this model to influence young people
and make him a thought leader for entire generations:
a model combining 'civil Islam,' in the terminology
of the RAND Corporation, with 'market Islam,'
in Patrick Haenni's terminology. This Islamic model
of civilization emphasizes
personal development, economic development,
and obedience to authority. At the same time, it is also
a religious model, not a secular one. This was the prevailing approach,
intended to empty Islam of its spirituality
and its civilizational dimension too, because civilization here is reduced
to economics and money. In any case,
I previously devoted an entire episode to discussing whether
Ahmad was a student of knowledge, when we discussed
his book Forty. We showed that he made disastrous errors
segments.review_notes: Book title 40 rendered Forty; allegations about its author remain the presenter's opinion.

segments.text: in creed and was not actually well read. We also
made an episode discussing and reviewing his entire approach,
so I recommend returning to it. We also devoted
a full episode to 'The Reality of Magic.' I cited
not only established revealed texts and scholars' statements,
but also evidence from other peoples unfamiliar with these
religions who were immersed in magic
and dealings with devils. In another episode, we discussed
jinn possession—more precisely, affliction,
segments.review_notes: Repeated مس in ASR reduced to meaningful repetition over two cues; audio needed to distinguish hesitation from caption artifact.

segments.text: affliction by jinn—and examined the Mu'tazilite views
being revived by this way of thinking, this so-called
modernist school, from Muhammad Abduh's time
to the present.
Let us now discuss the first question: is love
or romantic attachment between a human and a jinn possible? If you watched
the previous episodes, the answer will simply be yes,
without even needing research or evidence from religion and revelation,
or from elsewhere. This question, in itself,
is not about religion and revelation here, even though
revelation is, of course, the easiest and most reliable source
of information about the world of jinn. But
those who contact jinn through magic or other means,
including meditation, also reach these
conclusions and learn what can happen with this
world. Of course, we are not discussing
what is lawful or unlawful; that is a separate question. We are discussing
possibility alone. Quite simply, if
individuals from the two worlds can communicate,
regardless of the means and whether it is lawful,
then the outcomes of a social relationship between them
are possible: friendship, for example, or enmity; harm and deception
segments.review_notes: Damaged ASR من اء provisionally read as harm in the contrast with assistance; audio check required.

segments.text: by either party, or assistance and guidance
from either side, including guidance to the truth. Love, hatred,
romantic attachment and so on are all possible, as long as
communication is possible. The expression
'the enamoured jinn' is one of the most widely used terms
today. This exact expression was not known in our heritage.
Even if the term itself was not
in common use, the phenomenon was known, and there was no disagreement
about its possibility. What is meant here
segments.review_notes: The no-disagreement claim is translated as the speaker states it, not certified consensus.

segments.text: is a case of affliction: an enamoured jinn
afflicts a human it has fallen in love with.
It is not simply ordinary love; the familiar symptoms
of affliction are present. If anyone does not know what
affliction is, or its symptoms, I again refer you to our episode
on affliction and jinn possession of humans,
which we made two years ago. Since the jinn is usually
the one that sees the human, while humans can see
jinn only in very rare circumstances, as discussed earlier,
the relationship normally begins with the jinn.
I am speaking specifically about a relationship involving affliction,
an enamoured jinn. In some cases—and usually,
if not always, these do not involve Muslims; the afflicted person
segments.review_notes: ASR disfluent لم يكن دائما provisionally interpreted as إن لم يكن دائما, if not always. Audio review required; frequency and religious exclusions are speaker claims.

segments.text: is not Muslim—someone a jinn falls in love with may return
its feelings. The results are often disastrous.
Nevertheless, as I mentioned, there are cases where
the human begins it by initiating contact with those
worlds. This does not happen among Muslims,
but someone exploring meditation and energy practices
opens the door. Often, these things
happen in conjunction with drug use,
segments.review_notes: ASR فقط amid the phrase is unclear; translated as conjunction without asserting an exclusive causal rule. Audio review required.

segments.text: particular types of drugs. I may devote an episode entirely
to the spiritual relationship between drugs,
meditation and entering the worlds of jinn. This makes
it much easier, even without training. Suppose
a human—a man, for example—enters these worlds
through drugs and meditation, or even ordinary yoga
without any drugs. Once he enters that world,
a jinn may appear to him. It could be a male jinn appearing
as a woman, although that is rare; usually
a female jinn appears. What we described may then happen:
love and attachment. It may be seduction,
rather than genuine love on the other side. Every
possibility is open here. Imagine a relationship between
a man and a woman: all sorts of things can happen,
including deception, fraud, genuine love,
or exploitation of any kind. All are possible. I will give
just one example here. This image comes
from a spiritual Facebook page specializing
in drugs.
I will not name the page; I do not want to promote it.
If we make a separate episode about drugs,
I will show many examples from it. The page uses
humour, but it is based on realities:
segments.review_notes: Presenter calls the page factual; page and depicted image have not been independently inspected. Translation does not certify its claims.

segments.text: it describes what happens to them during meditation
combined with drugs. They call these 'trips,' journeys
into the spiritual world, but present them
as humorous memes. All the comments I see
on that page agree, from people who are also
addicted to these experiences: drugs and entering
these worlds, not simply for recreation,
but for a spiritual purpose. They see beings in all
the forms of jinn we discussed earlier. We will discuss
that later. For now, look at this example:
the drawing shows a man who has entered this world,
and these beings have come to him—'entities,'
the term they always use. They do not use
'demons' or 'devils'; they speak of entities.
These appear in different forms, including cases
where a being appears as a beautiful woman
and begins a romantic relationship with him. Here he says,
jokingly, 'I am tired of this love.
I do not want love; I want, for example,
some kind of spiritual relationship.' Let us return to affliction.
One of the best-known scholars to discuss affliction by
an enamoured jinn, describing it in those terms, is Ibn Taymiyyah.
In the same text we mentioned in the previous
section, Ibn Taymiyyah says that their affliction of humans
may arise from lust, desire and love, as happens between
segments.review_notes: ASR collapses وهوى وعشق into وهواشق; reading supported by the Ibn Taymiyyah passage previously inspected. Translation is an original paraphrase of the embedded quotation.

segments.text: humans. Then he mentions that humans
and jinn may intermarry, and so on. We should recall that in
a case of affliction, the jinn initiates it, whether male
or female. Again, a jinn has choice;
it is not compelled. It chooses disbelief, then chooses
to become a devil. It may subsequently
afflict someone, or be subjected through magic by a jinn sorcerer
segments.review_notes: ASR explicitly says جني ساحر (jinn sorcerer); retained despite possible intended human sorcerer. Check audio.

segments.text: and sent against that person. After the magic
and affliction, attachment may develop alongside the initial
case of magic, which has its own treatment. There may be
additional attachment—an additional problem. But in
other cases, a Muslim male or female jinn may become attached
to a Muslim man or woman. Even with faith,
attachment can occur. To understand this, it also happens
among Muslims: a Muslim human, even if sinful,
falls in love with a woman and may harm her or even
attempt rape or something else. So questions of faith
segments.review_notes: ASR فغطيه read contextually as فقضية, the question of. Audio check required.

segments.text: and being a devil do not exhaust the possibilities of affliction
and attachment. Practitioners of ruqyah also know that when
ruqyah begins and a male or female jinn speaks,
one of the first questions is, 'Are you Muslim?
If not, what is your religion?' A jinn can thus
be Muslim and still cause affliction and attachment. But
of course, a Muslim male or female jinn would not
segments.review_notes: Blanket characterization of Muslim jinn is the speaker's claim; not a new legal or theological verification.

segments.text: participate in magic. When there is possession through attachment,
there is a possibility that the male
or female jinn is Muslim. How do we recognize
this attachment-related affliction? It has the usual symptoms. Of course,
segments.review_notes: Following alleged signs and treatment references are a faithful research translation of the presenter, not diagnostic guidance or an editorial recommendation. The article separates these claims from medical evidence.

segments.text: an enamoured jinn appears to the person in dreams,
trying to seduce them. It usually appears either
as a handsome man to entice or seduce the targeted woman,
or conversely, as a beautiful woman to seduce
the targeted man. It may appear as someone
the target loves, someone they know personally
and are attached to, or as the target's husband or wife.
I know several cases, and will mention some accounts
I have received myself. Here is one example; we will come
to other stories later. One of my friends is a ruqyah practitioner,
deeply involved in the world of jinn, with more knowledge of it
than others. One day, a jinn appeared to him
in a dream as a beautiful young woman and tried
to seduce him. He was alert. Often, in these circumstances,
someone involved in this world
is in a state of partial awareness when these
interactions between worlds occur, although not always.
When she came and tried to seduce him, he recognized her
as a female jinn and refused her. She immediately changed
into her true form. We discussed
the various forms of jinn in an earlier episode. What is interesting—
or rather, unfortunate—is that she also tried
to hurt him: she gripped him tightly and tried to squeeze him,
letting out a shrill, screeching cry. That sound
has long been known, even among the Arabs
before Islam, as one of the reported sounds of jinn.
It resembles the whistling of wind or the sound of insects.
Even the word sarsur comes from this,
segments.review_notes: Sarsur left transliterated because ASR may mean cricket/cockroach; etymology and species identification unverified.

segments.text: because it makes a chirring sound. You also find this in some films
and animated works that have nothing to do
with religion or anything else. It is known as one
of the sounds of jinn. Some people may fall into the trap
in a dream and engage in forbidden acts, or they may not
be aware, as we said. So the question of what is lawful
segments.review_notes: ASR الحلاوه الحرام interpreted as الحلال والحرام from context. The speaker explicitly separates involuntary dream awareness from legal accountability.

segments.text: or unlawful is separate. But this often happens
at the beginning. Suppose, for example,
a beautiful woman appears to a young man and tries to seduce him,
and he does not know she is a jinn. This happens
in the early stages. But when someone becomes afflicted,
the targeting is clear and the experience recurs, whether
the female jinn appears in the same form each time or
in different forms. The afflicted person knows.
It may be confusing at first, but
almost always, as it continues, they eventually recognize it,
because it is accompanied by the other symptoms
of affliction: heaviness in the limbs,
other experiences while awake, and difficulty
reading the Qur'an or praying, and so on. There is
another point before we finish this section:
an enamoured jinn may remain attached to a victim for years
and destroy their life. It may prevent marriages
or cause an existing marriage
to fail.
This leads to hatred between spouses.
As I said, it may initially arise from magic,
magic intended to separate people, but it need not. A jinn
may become attached to a married woman simply because it loves her,
without any magic directed at her. To understand this better,
imagine someone whose life is targeted by a spy from an
intelligence agency, spying on them in order to
destroy their personal and married life. Imagine how
difficult that would be. Now imagine that
a female spy is assigned to a man and also falls in love with him,
wanting to take him away from his wife.
Imagine what that would be like in the human world.
What, then, of the world of jinn, when
this female jinn can enter his private life,
go into his bedroom with him, see him
in intimate circumstances, and visit him in dreams when
he is vulnerable and not fully conscious?
That is why I say this episode is very important: to understand
this subject and give everyone at least
a basic degree of protection against it.
And if it happens, God forbid, they should also have
enough knowledge of treatment.
Now for the episode's second question: if
an emotional relationship between the two kinds is possible,
segments.review_notes: ASR الجنس سين interpreted as الجنسين, the two kinds (humans and jinn), not male/female sexes.

segments.text: is a physical, intimate relationship possible? Once
again, children must not listen to this episode.
We will speak
with as little explicit detail as possible, while also
being clear enough for people
to understand. We all know that purely chaste love,
even among us humans, is a myth. When a man
segments.review_notes: Presenter's generalization about chaste love preserved as speech, not editorial fact.

segments.text: becomes attached to a woman and loves her, it is natural to think
segments.review_notes: ASR عرق interpreted contextually as تعلق/عرف; translation expresses attachment without asserting recovered audio wording.

segments.text: beyond that, about a physical relationship. That is
what we know between the sexes among humans.
So if love is possible between humans
and jinn, it naturally leads to
the possibility of an intimate relationship between them.
The main question is how this would happen. We are discussing
two different worlds: humans are material beings, while jinn
are from fire. In an earlier episode, I said
we cannot understand precisely the nature
of their bodies or how they were created from fire, and so on.
With two different worlds and natures, how could
such a relationship occur? There are two ways. In the first,
a male or female jinn takes bodily form
as a human man or woman and enters our world
to have this relationship with the targeted person.
Briefly, Imam al-Suyuti, in his book Laqt
al-marjan fi ahkam al-jann, mentioned several stories of male
jinn proposing to human women through
their families. Questions were put to the sheikhs of that
age, and all the rulings prohibited it.
segments.review_notes: Blanket claims about rulings and historical unanimity remain unverified; Laqt original edition is pending.

segments.text: No one said it was impossible; they said
the marriage was unlawful. The book also mentions
female jinn appearing to men, followed by actual marriages.
But all these stories lack chains of transmission. They might
be true, but appear to be legends. I also said earlier
segments.review_notes: Presenter qualifies the stories as lacking chains and apparently legendary; preserve alongside possibility claims.

segments.text: that a jinn taking bodily form in our world requires
segments.review_notes: Embodiment-energy and duration claims are the speaker's hypothesis, not established physics.

segments.text: a great deal of energy to enter
this world, and does not last long: minutes or seconds,
not hours. It consumes its energy and must
return to its world. But in principle, nothing
prevents this relationship from occurring, even if
the bodily appearance lasts only minutes. In principle,
nothing prevents a relationship during those minutes
with a different kind of being that has taken
our form. I have also heard stories
from people I know about people they know,
all trustworthy, God willing, describing
physical contact between a human and a jinn that had taken
human form, even embracing. Not a man
embracing a woman: there was no question of love here. These
are accounts I know and consider confirmed: when it takes bodily form,
segments.review_notes: Confirmed here translates the presenter's own confidence, not registry verification of testimony.

segments.text: you can hold it,
as though it were an ordinary person. But remember, this
embodiment is very limited and consumes energy.
Could it lead to intercourse? It is possible
in principle, but I have no account confirming
segments.review_notes: Essential negative testimony retained: presenter has no account confirming physical intercourse.

segments.text: that it has happened. Now, suppose it appears
to someone in its true form, or even
in another form, visible only to the targeted
person and resembling a shadow. We discussed this
in detail in earlier episodes. In that case,
physical contact does not occur. It is like a shadow, ghost
or apparition, so intercourse cannot occur
in that state; it must take bodily form. There is another question:
can a jinn share in a man's intercourse
with his wife? Some religious books mention this
if the man does not invoke Allah's name—does not say 'Bismillah'—
at intercourse. These are weak reports.
segments.review_notes: These unspecified weak reports must remain distinct from the sound protective supplication in Bukhari 141.

segments.text: That is a separate subject; I mention it only
as a reminder. The second possibility is that
intercourse occurs in the world of spirits, either during
meditation with drugs among people entering the world
of energy practices, usually non-Muslims, or during
dreams. These cases are confirmed [laughs]; there is no
segments.review_notes: Speaker calls these experiences confirmed; no independent clinical or supernatural-cause verification. Laughter marker retained from ASR.

segments.text: disagreement about them. I also know people with accounts
we will come to later. Can a person be
raped by these beings, these jinn,
in their dreams? Very briefly, the answer is that if
they are non-Muslim and immersed in sin, they can be raped,
segments.review_notes: Speaker's claim concerning non-Muslims and sin; must not be adopted as editorial causation or victim blame.

segments.text: yes; we will mention cases. If the person is Muslim,
it is possible in principle, just as we say a Muslim woman may
be raped by a wicked, immoral, unbelieving man.
Her Islam and faith do not necessarily protect her. A person can
be killed, defrauded, robbed
or raped even if devout, and be tested
by that. It is a trial. So, in principle,
and in real life, faith and Islam may not protect someone,
although it may be more likely that Allah protects them
and they are not harmed. But no text says faith
will protect you. By the same reasoning, in principle,
faith would not necessarily protect you against something
segments.review_notes: Disfluent ASR rendered as not necessarily protected, maintaining the preceding explicit statement that devout people can be assaulted.

segments.text: like this in dreams. However, according to my information,
the accounts I know from other people,
specialists and ruqyah practitioners, there is not a single case
happening in this way. A Muslim woman,
even if she falls short in religious practice, simply by
being Muslim has something protecting her in dreams
segments.review_notes: Protection claim is attributed speech based on contacts; it is not a scriptural guarantee. Article must preserve the prior limitation and avoid blaming victims.

segments.text: from the enamoured jinn reaching the point of
completed rape. But it will harass and hurt her, and so on.
Now I will tell some stories. Listen without
being afraid; we listen only to understand and protect ourselves.
This is simply awareness. In the stories I mention,
I will not reveal people's identities, of course, or disclose
their secrets. The first concerns a widow. She is not
young; she has children,
but is not currently married. She comes from a respected
family I know, and I know this is
a trustworthy source. It is an older story, which I heard
some time ago. For many years, she had nightmares.
She had not thought of seeking a sheikh's help because she believed
it was not serious. Unfortunately, that is common.
Every few months she would have these dreams,
and came to suspect that an enamoured jinn was targeting her.
But as I said, it did not trouble her much,
so she tried to live with it, using Qur'an recitation, ruqyah,
and so on. She did not approach a ruqyah practitioner
to rid her of it permanently. I always say in
my episodes that I am not a sheikh, counsellor or
ruqyah practitioner, so I do not accept consultations
about this. She knows that. But she said that after
watching our episodes some months earlier about the world
of jinn, affliction, the reality of magic and other subjects,
she saw me in a dream, without intending or seeking
to do so. In one dream, I appeared
to her and tried to perform ruqyah for her. She said
I began reciting it while she was aware,
but did not finish. Then the devil that
always targeted her appeared. That is why she contacted me,
saying, 'I want you to finish the ruqyah
you began in the dream.' I told her,
'I do not know specific ruqyahs or practise them myself, but
I have a collection of well-known ones available
online. Search for them and you will find dozens
of verses and remembrances everyone knows.'
I told her to recite them and make sure to read Ayat
al-Kursi before sleeping. We must bring reverence
segments.review_notes: Devotional advice in the narrated account is not proof of treatment efficacy. Energy terminology is the presenter's own self-correction.

segments.text: and spiritual energy—or spiritual strength
from faith—to its recitation. Not everyone
who recites it receives its blessing with the same
strength. You must be attentive and reflect on the verse
while reading it, and sleep in a state of ablution, alongside ruqyah,
reciting al-Baqarah, and so on. I also advised her
to find a practitioner in her own country to perform ruqyah

contain many similar stories, most famously
Zeus, chief and greatest of the gods, the god
of the sky—Iblis himself. The story, or myth,
segments.review_notes: Zeus=Iblis is the speaker's interpretation, not established scriptural identification.

segments.text: says he married and seduced dozens of human women,
who bore him beings described as demigods,
including Heracles—Hercules—and Helen,
among others. In medieval Europe,
we also have the incubus and succubus, as discussed.
The incubus in particular is a devil
that feeds on the sexual energy of the woman
it targets in her dreams. What is striking in all these
legends is that this devil does not merely feed
on her energy; it drains her. So
a woman experiencing this kind of affliction—
these are not legends; they are mentioned in their religious
segments.review_notes: Speaker shifts from legends to religious-book claims; both statements retained.

segments.text: books, Christian books, as I said—
if a woman actually experiences this targeting
and takeover over a period of
years, or even months, it drains her mental,
psychological and physical energy, and she often dies afterward.
segments.review_notes: No mortality rate or clinical evidence is supplied. This is the presenter's unverified prognosis claim, not medical guidance.

segments.text: This is also what we know in our own world. I
recently heard a very painful story,
told by a sister about a woman she knew, a friend,
who died by suicide after prolonged affliction by an enamoured jinn.
segments.review_notes: Anonymous third-hand report; suicide causation not independently established. Kept in full research translation but omitted from condensed article; no method described.

segments.text: So I repeat: this subject deserves attention and calls for
treatment for anyone affected, God forbid. Also,
the hybrid figure, the cambion, appears frequently
in anime and comics, and unfortunately
in popular culture today. Many
young people follow these without knowing their danger. Let us turn
to some modern films about
similar accounts. There is a well-known documentary entitled
The Nightmare, which I cited in several
earlier episodes. Its American director, Rodney Ascher,
said he made it because he himself
had experienced nightmares for several years. He is of
Jewish origin and non-religious; he always says he is agnostic,
segments.review_notes: Claims about Ascher's ancestry/religion are unverified. Inspected Sundance interview expresses uncertainty about experiences' origin, not proof of these biographical claims.

segments.text: non-religious, uncertain. He says, 'I want to believe,'
but has no belief in anything. He says
he experienced nightmares and made this film, interviewing
eight Americans without belief
segments.review_notes: Claim that all eight participants were American and non-religious is not independently checked; original film review pending.

segments.text: in any religion, all experiencing affliction.
Some came to believe. For example, a man named Chris said
that this spiritual experience
of nightmares and possession led him
to abandon atheism and believe in God's existence.
Another participant, Connie,
segments.review_notes: Chris/Connie religious-change accounts require original film timestamps and attribution checks.

segments.text: said her years of experiences with
sleep paralysis led her back
to Christianity and away from atheism, because Christian
treatment was what healed her. An important question
may arise here, which I may have discussed more than once:
how can a Christian priest heal or treat someone
and free them from a devil? Very briefly,
first, this is a religion that has been altered. A Christian believes
in Allah, but associates Jesus, peace be upon him, with Him.
Some Gospel passages contain true revelation,
while others have been altered. Also, any spiritual treatment,
even within a religion that is fundamentally false, contains spiritual strength.
segments.review_notes: Cross-religious efficacy and spiritual-strength explanation are presenter's claims, not clinical findings.

segments.text: That strength may actually produce treatment,
even without Qur'an or Gospel. Thus, even in
Hinduism and Buddhism, magical incantations are used
to treat magic. We also have nushrah,
segments.review_notes: Nushrah is undoing alleged sorcery; types, conditions and legal disagreement require separate sources. Do not render as blanket permission for magical treatment.

segments.text: which may use recitations
not drawn from the Qur'an, yet achieve the result,
treatment, and may be lawful. The point is that participants
in this film literally say the beings appearing
in their dreams are 'shadow people.'
As I said earlier, when a devil appears to us
without full embodiment, it is like a ghost, apparition or shadow.
What matters here is that one woman in the film says
segments.review_notes: This participant is unnamed in transcript; do not merge her with Connie without checking original film.

segments.text: an evil being raped her. She does not
use the terms jinn or devils. She felt

everything. She was rigid and helpless,
unable to move any part of her body, while it could
do whatever it wanted. Similar stories appear in many
Hollywood films. One example is
The Entity, reportedly based on a true story.
segments.review_notes: ASR film name damaged; The Entity identified from context and existing registry. True-story claim means reportedly based on an account, not independently verified assault causation.

she suffered assaults by ghosts in

four years later, in 1982, the film appeared,

segments.text: also under that title. Again, 'entity'

They do not know the term jinn; they speak of spiritual beings
that appear and may be good or evil. The film's story

is taken over by this entity, which rapes her,
and the story continues. A new version of this film

initially appearing

The story then develops further. There is also
a film released in 1985, Lifeforce.
A space mission discovers a spacecraft
containing frozen alien beings and brings them
to Earth. One is female. When she
awakens, she becomes a vampire and begins
physical relationships with humans to absorb their energy.
The same idea, but with aliens. As we said
earlier, aliens are jinn. There is also
segments.review_notes: Equating aliens with jinn is the speaker's interpretation, not independent identification of fictional beings.

which draws on the same incubus,
the nightmare-spirit. Briefly, a couple moves

raping her in her sleep, then taking over

released in 1968: Rosemary's Baby. It is still
considered a horror classic. Its story
is different, but briefly, a couple moves
into an apartment in a New York building
with a recurring reputation for being haunted.
An elderly couple lives next door; they belong
to a secret satanic sect. This sect
looks for a woman meeting certain conditions
required by Satan himself, Iblis, so he can rape her
or have intercourse with her without her awareness. She then becomes pregnant and bears him
the Antichrist, who will lead humanity at the end
segments.review_notes: Speaker says المسيح الدجال. Antichrist renders his description in this Western-fiction context; this does not equate the fictional child with Islam's Dajjal. Film-source record does not establish that identification.

segments.text: of time. The whole story revolves around this, ending
with his success: she gives birth to
the Antichrist. What is striking about all these films
is their agreement on the possibility of sex and intercourse between
humans and jinn, even though, as we said, the Christian
and Jewish West does not recognize jinn as this distinct kind
of being, instead considering them fallen angels. Also,
people who do not accept Judaism or Christianity speak of
'entities,' beings capable of having
segments.review_notes: Damaged ASR وكانات ذديز interpreted as repeated English entities and Arabic beings; audio review required.

segments.text: these relationships with humans, with or without

to do this with them to draw
energy from them. As we said, this is also familiar among

exploring this world through energy practices and entering
other worlds to expand their awareness:
if you are Muslim, you must know these are jinn and devils,
and no lawful relationship can be established with them.
If it reaches intercourse, that is zina,
segments.review_notes: Closing prohibition addresses deliberate pursuit of contact; earlier sleeping-person exemption (844–845) and assault accounts must not be erased or converted into blame.

segments.text: even in another world: unlawful sex, a grave indecency.
So be extremely cautious about entering this world,
even out of curiosity. Anyone who, God forbid,
has been afflicted in this way should heed the advice
I have repeated throughout this episode: go immediately
to a sheikh and begin treatment and ruqyah. If you cannot
segments.review_notes: Presenter's advice preserved in research translation; no independent treatment efficacy, diagnosis, or recommendation to discontinue professional care.

begin reciting ruqyah while you keep looking. Search
online; you will find many recitations and the methods
I mentioned, including applying oil, and so on. The point is
not to postpone or underestimate this matter.
I ask Allah to protect us all and preserve us from
every harm. Thank you for listening. Peace be upon you,
and [Allah's] mercy.
